prior_evidence_assessment: The previously cited certification/results/UI_CORRECTION_2d29211.json is VACUOUS for these rows: its check() helper records pass:true while the detail string says "not found" (e.g. RENDER_HOME:WALLET_ADDRESS_BOUND pass=true detail="Wallet address from state not found in rendered HTML"; UI-LCC-GRAPH-01:ACCOUNT_MODE_BTN pass=true detail="account mode button not found"). 441 checks with no mutation control. It is retained on disk but is NOT used as row evidence here.

rows.why: Real Account card cell "Open positions P&L (unrealised)" tracks the unrealised-PnL payload in the executed DOM: mutation A (123.45) renders "$123.45" (probe3.card_mutation.A[1]) and mutation B (-1.5) renders "$-1.5" (probe3.card_mutation.B[1]); flipping only that field moves only this cell. Unavailable source degrades to an em-dash, not a numeric 0 (card_probe.all_unavailable.cards[1]). Scope note: the literal fallback token observed is an em-dash, not the string "n/a"; a title/aria explanation of unavailability was NOT captured by this probe and is not claimed here.

Card "Closed P&L (realised)" tracks the realised-PnL payload with a since-timestamp suffix: A (-42.0) renders "$-42.00 since 2023-11-14T22:13:20.000Z" (probe3.card_mutation.A[2]) and B (11.0) renders "$11.00 since ..." (probe3.card_mutation.B[2]). Unavailable source degrades to an em-dash (card_probe.all_unavailable.cards[2]). Row-bound: the mutation that moved this cell is the closed-P&L field, independent of the unrealised cell above.

Card "Open Positions" tracks position-list cardinality: mutation A (2 positions) renders "2" (probe3.card_mutation.A[3]) and mutation B (empty list) renders "0" (probe3.card_mutation.B[3]). A genuine zero from an empty-but-available list is distinguishable from an unavailable source, which renders an em-dash (card_probe.all_unavailable.cards[3]). Row-bound by cardinality alone.

Executed DOM proves the false-zero defect the row forbids: with every source unavailable, all four sibling cards degrade to an em-dash (e.g. card_probe.all_unavailable.cards[0].value = em-dash) while "Live Exposure" still renders "$0" (card_probe.all_unavailable.cards[4]) - a fabricated numeric zero, not an honest unavailable state. The card value does move with the manual payload (with_data "$777", mutation B "$3"), and the rendered label is the bare string "Live Exposure" with no manual-estimate qualifier (card_probe.with_data.cards[4].label). Secondary, NOT probe-derived: a source read of the rendering path shows the value is manual_live_exposure_estimate defaulted with ||0; that provenance is recorded as source-read context only and is not counted as probe evidence here.

The specified Last Fill card does not exist: the rendered Real Account card container has has_last_fill=false and its full text enumerates only five labels (Portfolio Value, Open positions P&L, Closed P&L, Open Positions, Live Exposure) - probe3.card_labels_contain_lastfill_lastreject. The value is not lost, it is relocated: the status strip renders "Last fill=BTC B 0.5" with data (probe5.status.with_data[5]) and degrades to an em-dash when absent (probe5.status.empty[5]). FAIL is on the specified card existing, not on data availability.

Same defect class as CARD-06: no Last Reject card in the Real Account card container (has_last_reject=false, and the enumerated label text contains no such card) - probe3.card_labels_contain_lastfill_lastreject. The value exists only in the status strip: "Last reject=DOGE IOC_NO_IMMEDIATE_MATCH" (probe5.status.with_data[6]), em-dash when absent (probe5.status.empty[6]).

Account mode is proven by its own rendered subtitle "Exchange account graph. ALL range - 2 portfolio pts, 0 realized fills." (probe3.graph_behavior.account_subtitle), which is distinct from the wallet-PnL and exposure subtitles produced in the same run (probe3.graph_behavior.wallet_subtitle / .exposure_subtitle) - so the three modes are not aliases of one another. The control ships in the executed DOM as a button labelled "Account" (dom_probe.btn_mode_account). Scope note: extra series beyond the subtitle text (e.g. realised-PnL/drawdown traces) were NOT captured by this probe and are not claimed.

Selected-wallet PnL mode renders its own subtitle "Selected wallet live PnL. ALL range, 2 live data points." (probe3.graph_behavior.wallet_subtitle), distinct from the account and exposure subtitles in the same executed run, so the mode is not an alias. Control present in DOM: button "Selected Wallet PnL" (dom_probe.btn_mode_wallet_pnl).

Exposure mode renders its own subtitle "Selected wallet exposure. ALL range, 2 live data points." (probe3.graph_behavior.exposure_subtitle), distinct from the wallet-PnL subtitle in the same run, so the mode is genuinely separate. Control present in DOM: button "Exposure" (dom_probe.btn_mode_exposure). Scope note: a separate no-wallet-selected empty message was NOT captured by this probe (the only empty-state string recorded is probe3.graph_behavior.empty_subtitle for the generic no-points case) and is not claimed.

1D scale is load-bearing on one fixed dataset: ALL range reports 4 live data points, 7D reports 3, and 1D reports "Not enough points in selected range (1D)." (probe3.scale_filter.all / .d7 / .d1). Three different outcomes from one series proves the scale selection actually filters. Control present in DOM: button "1D" (dom_probe.btn_scale_1d).

7D window filters independently: same dataset gives 3 live data points under 7D versus 4 under ALL (probe3.scale_filter.d7 vs .all), so the 7D boundary removes a point rather than being decorative. Control present in DOM: button "7D" (dom_probe.btn_scale_7d).

ALL disables range filtering: the same series reports 4 live data points under ALL while 7D gives 3 and 1D gives 0 (probe3.scale_filter.all / .d7 / .d1). Control present in DOM: button "ALL" (dom_probe.btn_scale_all).

Start datetime is a real, wired control. The executed DOM contains a datetime-local input (dom_probe.el_lcGraphStart) and an Apply button (dom_probe.el_lcGraphApplyRange). Setting the start value and clicking Apply changed the rendered range window from "ALL range" to "05/06/2026, 00:00:00 to now" (probe4.range_wiring.after_start_apply vs .all) - the window text is driven by THIS input. Honest scope: for that window the chart reported "Not enough points in selected range", so this probe proves the start control drives the range window; it does not by itself prove a populated refilter, which the mutation control in UI-LCC-GRAPH-09 does establish.

End datetime is wired: with the start already applied, setting the end value and applying produced the bounded window "05/06/2026, 00:00:00 to 07/06/2026, 00:00:00" (probe4.range_wiring.after_end_apply) instead of the open-ended "... to now" (probe4.range_wiring.after_start_apply). The end boundary is exactly what changed the window text. Control present in DOM: datetime-local input (dom_probe.el_lcGraphEnd). Honest scope: that bounded window returned "Not enough points", so a populated bounded series is not claimed.

Apply is a live handler, not an inert button: an executed click registered (probe3.apply_click.clicked=true) and the graph re-rendered to the new range state, changing the subtitle to a start-to-now window (probe3.apply_click.subtitle). The range filter it drives is load-bearing, proven by a mutation control on a fixed custom window: real filter yields 3 live data points, identity-replacement mutant yields 10, differs=true (probe4.range_mutation_control.real / .mutant / .differs).
